valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date)

bear.driver: Class 8 truck cycle softening, supplier/component constraints, and margin compression

base.driver: Normalized 2027 truck build rates, resilient PACCAR Parts growth (3-5%), and stable Financial Services pretax income

bull.driver: Emissions-standard pre-buy tailwinds, stronger Class 8 demand, and operating leverage

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $6.75, the $106.66 close implies 15.8x P/E; the Street consensus target range ($125.10-$131.96) implies 18.5x-19.5x base EPS or $7.15-$7.54 EPS at 17.5x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $6.75 (6.3 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Quarterly Class 8 truck deliveries (Q4 2026 guidance: 41,000-43,000 units) and PACCAR Parts revenue growth.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 / FY2026 earnings release (expected late January 2027)

analyst_notes: Following Q3 2026 earnings on October 27, 2026 ($1.61 diluted EPS, record $1.78B Parts revenue, 40,100 truck deliveries), named analysts trimmed price targets to reflect near-term supply constraints and cyclical moderation while largely maintaining constructive ratings for 2027 (Evercore ISI cut from $162 to $134, JPMorgan from $142 to $132, Truist from $125 to $124). Street targets ($124-$134 among these named calls) sit above our $118.13 base case (+10.8% vs. $106.66 close), implying either a higher 18.5x-19.5x multiple on $6.75 EPS or stronger FY2027 EPS.
